The review guidance defines absent as not registered, or with its outline or steps content missing or out of order. The failure must be a non-zero exit at a check that reports the sample as missing or not matching the outline, and the output must name the failed phase. The quoted verifier has these checks, all labelled with the &#39;sample&#39; phase. (1) After the build and before the preview starts, it fails when the reference slug is not registered in src/presentations/index.ts (verify.mjs:97-101). (2) In the and-scene package, it fails when scripts/reference-outline.json is missing (verify.mjs:28-30). (3) It fails when the rendered step count differs from the reference outline (verify.mjs:54-56). (4) It fails when any step&#39;s title or caption does not match the outline in order (verify.mjs:61-67). The top-level handler prints &#39;[verify] FAIL (&lt;phase&gt;)&#39; and sets process.exitCode = 1 (verify.mjs:123-127). This satisfies &#39;non-zero exit whose output names the build or sample phase&#39;. The E2E-002 tests cover three faults: an unregistered sample, a deleted outline with the sample removed from the registry, and an out-of-order outline. Each test asserts a non-zero exit, &#39;[verify] FAIL (sample)&#39;, and the matching message (verify.test.mjs:55-91, 128-138). The guidance does not require a dedicated test when the check is explicit, but these tests exist anyway. One edge case remains: emptying the whole OUTLINE array while keeping the sample registered. That edge case does not undercut the ruling. The quoted code gives no evidence that it would end only in an unrelated timeout: Presentation.tsx:36-45 reads step.id from steps[0], and verify.mjs:39 and 47-49 would report the uncaught page error at step 0. Three automated tests drive a browser, each by running the project&#39;s own Playwright scripts as a subprocess: tests/e2e/verify.test.mjs (runs scripts/verify.mjs), tests/integration/inspect.test.mjs (runs scripts/inspect-presentation.mjs) and tests/integration/bootstrap.test.mjs (runs `npm run verify` in a scaffolded app). A search of every *.test.* file finds no other test that uses chromium, playwright, waitForTimeout or sleep. All three files are quoted in full. None of them contains a fixed sleep. Every assertion comes after `await run(...)`, and tests/helpers.mjs `run` resolves only on the child&#39;s &#39;close&#39; event. The setTimeout in `run` is a SIGKILL safety timeout that is cleared on close, not a wait. The only other setTimeout in a test (verify.test.mjs:111) is text inside an injected fault string, written into SampleScene.tsx to cause an uncaught page error. The test does not wait on it. Inside the driven script, each wait for state is a polling wait with a timeout: waitForSelector(&#39;[data-step-count]&#39;) and, after each ArrowRight, waitForFunction on data-step-index === n (verify.mjs:44-84). Judge C points to the waitForTimeout(SETTLE_MS) at verify.mjs:69. That call is in the verification script, not a test. It also runs only after the step index has been reached through waitForFunction and after the step index (line 59-60), title and caption (lines 61-68) have been checked. So it is not a fixed sleep used in place of waiting for a transition before asserting the step, which is the case the guidance says fails. It is a short window for catching late errors before assertClean, and nothing in the requirement depends on it. Judge C&#39;s reason therefore does not decide this criterion. In the inspect test, the `--settle` value is a minimum settle interval. Its assertions (inspect.test.mjs:92-101) check that capture waited past both the interval and the entity motion, not that a fixed delay happened.","evidence":["tests/e2e/verify.test.mjs:1-140, full file. `verify` runs scripts/verify.mjs through run(). The material doesn&#39;t establish that, and the guidance doesn&#39;t name it, so under the judging rules it cannot fail the criterion. If the preview process exits, the loop throws on the early exit. Refused connections are caught and retried until the deadline. The auditor concedes the build-before-preview clause is met. The printed-URL parsing clause does not apply because readiness doesn&#39;t read printed output.
